items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewer mentions Blackwell in the context of Ornette Coleman's band, and the interviewee agrees ('Oh yeah'), but the interviewee does not describe a personal or professional relationship with Blackwell.

ctx.x: We'd listened to some of the records, and yeah, when Ornette came out, that was a big jolt to doing what we were, to freeing a person up. Although Ornette's was really very structured but it sounded freer than people gave it credit for…

Than it actually was because, you know. Me, personally I think it's a misnomer when you say "Free Jazz." All the horns and the basses are playing free with Eric and all of them but Blackwell and Higgins are playing time, pretty much all the way through.
